description: The Department of Justice released an incomplete set of documents on Friday, in a violation of the 30-day window specified by the Epstein Files Transparency Act. Attorney General Pam Bondi promised that the additional documents would be delivered within two weeks.
headline: Department of Justice Partially Releases Documents in Partial Accordance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act

info.description: The Act did not specify a punishment in the event that the letter of the law is not followed.
info.note: Act co-author Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) warned previously before the release that anyone obstructing the full release of the files would likely be charged by a different administration.

info.description: The Department of Justice notably did not include a press release as part of this effort.
info.note: This is despite releasing eight other press releases that day.

info.description: Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche indicated the morning of release on a Fox News interview that the files would be incomplete.
info.note: He went on to state that there would be no favoritism in redaction shown and that the delay was owing to that care was being taken to redact victims' names.

info.description: Oversight Ranking Member Robert Garcia (D-CA) and Judiciary Ranking Member Jamie Raskin (D-MD) released a joint statement after Todd Blanche's interview.
info.note: They state that they are "now examining all legal options in the face of this violation of federal law."

info.description: Many online commentators expressed frustration at the extensive redactions present in the December 19 release.
info.note: Some documents are redacted nearly in full.
